input.rationale: Recovery/context-validity question on hashicorp/raft: after a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, does the node's in-memory configuration still reflect the committed configuration retained in its own log? Receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 (exit 0) now answers the two declared comparisons completely: with the flag on, the restarted node reports latest configuration index 0 and no voter (both assertions violated, witness event index 1) although it restored commit index 11 over 12 log entries; with the flag off the same restart reports index 1 with one voter (assertion holds, evaluated event index 3). Source reading gives the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct; restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other, but it starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The remaining open gap - a committed configuration entry newer than the on-disk snapshot - is addressed by the second experiment submitted here, which raises SnapshotThreshold so a snapshot exists, commits an AddNonvoter configuration change and then enough further entries that the change falls below the restored commit index.

investigations.question: After a restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and a CommitTrackingLogStore, is the node's in-memory configuration still the committed configuration retained in its own log?
investigations.hypothesis: restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup configuration scan, so the scan bound max(snapshotIndex, lastappliedIndex)+1 skips committed LogConfiguration entries and r.configurations keeps the snapshot (or empty) value.
investigations.discriminator: Restart the same single-node state twice from identical stores, once with RestoreCommittedLogs on and once off, and compare configuration index, server count and hasVote(local) observed immediately after NewRaft returns; the cases differ only in whether lastApplied was advanced by restoreFromCommittedLogs.

knowledge.statement: At startup the in-memory configuration (r.configurations.latest/committed) is produced only by restoreSnapshot (the latest snapshot's configuration) and by the NewRaft log scan over indexes greater than max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied). With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, restoreFromCommittedLogs sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index before that scan, so a committed LogConfiguration entry at an index <= the restored commit index is never processed and the node keeps the snapshot configuration, or an empty configuration when no snapshot exists.
knowledge.conditions: Config.RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a LogStore implementing CommitTrackingLogStore; the persisted commit index from GetCommitIndex is at least the index of the latest committed LogConfiguration entry; no snapshot covers that entry (no snapshot at all, or snapshot.ConfigurationIndex below it).

gaps.question: Does the same loss of configuration occur when a snapshot exists whose configuration index is below the index of a committed LogConfiguration entry (entries in (snapshotIndex, restored commitIndex])?

interpretations.rationale: Receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 (exit 0, four events, no parse loss) establishes both declared comparisons completely. Comparison 0 (mode on, no snapshot): the asserted predicate after_latest_index == before_latest_index is contradicted by witness event index 1, which reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false, after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, having been admitted by event index 0 (before_latest_index 1, one server, snapshots 0); comparison 1 (mode on, after_has_vote true) is likewise violated by the same witness. Comparison 2 is the control: with RestoreCommittedLogs off the same restart satisfies after_latest_index == 1 and the event carries one voter, so the restart itself, the stores and the applied entries are not the cause. The earlier receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f carries the same two result events but its comparisons were declared with an identity that could not correlate admission and result, so those outcomes were unknown; the raw events are retained there and are not used as a completed comparison. Source mechanism: NewRaft begins with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but starts at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1, and restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before it and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below that index are never processed; processLogs only forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM and never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). Consequence: the restarted node's own membership view is the snapshot's or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) leave it unable to campaign, and quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) is computed over a configuration that contradicts the node's committed log. The registered gap remains open here: the snapshot-present case is submitted as the second experiment and its receipt is required before that variant can be interpreted.

ef5ddbf78bd4456ea51537bd60a61a80-gap-0.explanation: Partially advanced: a single-voter run without any snapshot is witnessed as violated by receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175, and the snapshot-present variant is submitted as a second experiment whose receipt is still required before this gap can be resolved.

counterevidence: The control case in the same receipt (RestoreCommittedLogs off) keeps the committed configuration, isolating the flagged recovery path.

A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex; this does not cover a configuration committed after the snapshot, which is what the second experiment checks.
limitations: The witnessed case is a single-voter configuration with no snapshot; broader membership consequences (for example elections run under a stale configuration) are argued from the code but not witnessed.
The snapshot-present variant is not yet resolved by a receipt.
The unrelated suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts is untested and outside this claim.
interpretations.joint_history: Receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f and receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 both executed the same fixed inputs (same harness file, same single-node bootstrapped configuration with CommitTrackingLogs, same ten applied entries, same restart from the identical logs/stable/snapshots stores) and emitted four events with matching identities and matching operand values: mode on gave after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false and mode off gave 1, 1, true in both receipts. They are not fragments of one history: each receipt is a self-contained execution of the whole scenario, and the second one exists only because the comparison declaration changed (identity_fields reduced to mode); the first receipt's raw events are cited as observations, and only the second receipt's comparison outcomes are used as the completed comparison.

scope.description: Single-node bootstrapped cluster with RestoreCommittedLogs on and a CommitTrackingLogStore. Commit enough entries that a snapshot is taken, then commit an AddNonvoter configuration change (which commits with a one-voter quorum) and ten further commands so the persisted commit index moves past the configuration entry. Restart from the same stores and compare the configuration held after NewRaft returns with the configuration the log says is latest.
assumptions: The snapshot on disk carries only the bootstrap configuration, so it cannot represent the later AddNonvoter change.
Committing the nonvoter does not change the quorum, so the single voter keeps making progress.
The persisted commit index has advanced past the configuration entry's index by the time of the restart.
excluded: Any change of production logic; only the library's public configuration API and test facilities are used.
The unrelated suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts.

experiment.prefix: The harness boots one node with CommitTrackingLogs and a low SnapshotThreshold, repeats Apply until snapshots.List() returns a snapshot, then calls AddNonvoter, awaits its IndexFuture, and commits ten more commands so the staged commit index passes the configuration entry. It emits a startup_before_restart event carrying the snapshot index, the snapshot's configuration index, the configuration entry index and the expected server count, then shuts the node down and calls NewRaft again on the same logs, stable and snapshots stores with a fresh inmem transport. The restart_after_config_change event reports the configuration observed after NewRaft returns together with the operands of the comparison (expected and actual index and server count, restored commit index, lastApplied).
experiment.responsibility: The library owns the precondition that a node's in-memory configuration reflects the committed configuration in its own log at startup, including changes newer than the snapshot; the caller selects Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and triggers the change through the public API.

comparisons.description: After restarting from a state whose log holds a committed configuration change newer than the snapshot, the node's latest configuration index and server count are expected to equal the ones the log established before shutdown; the defect prediction is that the node falls back to the snapshot's configuration.
The restarted node is expected to still list the added nonvoter, i.e. two servers against the snapshot's one; the defect prediction is one server.

scope.description: Bootstrap a single-node cluster whose LogStore is a CommitTrackingLogStore, commit ten commands (leaving the bootstrap LogConfiguration at index 1 committed), shut the node down without any snapshot, restart it from the identical logs/stable/snapshots stores and emit the configuration observed immediately after NewRaft returns. Run the identical sequence twice, with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs true and false.
assumptions: The in-memory commit-tracking store stands in for a durable CommitTrackingLogStore per the interface contract in log.go:194-219.
No snapshot is taken, so the snapshot path cannot supply a configuration.
Restarting a one-node configuration is a legal deployment of the library; the difference between the two cases is only whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied.
excluded: Whole-package or repository test suites; only the two named cases run.
Any snapshot-present scenario, which is left to the registered gap.
The separate suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts.

basis.prefix: The harness uses the package's own test facilities: inmemConfig, MakeClusterOpts{Peers:1, Bootstrap:true, CommitTrackingLogs:true} and MakeClusterCustom, so BootstrapCluster writes the LogConfiguration entry at index 1 and NewRaft runs the real startup path. SnapshotThreshold/SnapshotInterval/TrailingLogs are raised so no snapshot exists. Ten Apply calls are awaited, then the node is Shutdown and NewRaft is called again with the same logs, stable and snapshots stores and a fresh inmem transport, as the package's own restart test does. The event is emitted after NewRaft returns; no leader-dependent step is assumed at restart time. The harness first emits a startup_before_restart event describing the committed configuration index and server count observed before shutdown (the setup the result event depends on), then the restart_after_recovery result event; both events carry the same mode/phase identity so the two cases stay distinguishable.
basis.responsibility: The library owns the precondition that a node's in-memory configuration reflects the committed configuration in its own log at startup; the caller only selects Config.RestoreCommittedLogs and supplies a CommitTrackingLogStore.

comparisons.description: With RestoreCommittedLogs on and no snapshot, the restarted node's latest configuration index is expected to equal the committed configuration index observed before the restart (1); the defect prediction is that it is 0.

Control: with RestoreCommittedLogs off the same restart is expected to keep the committed configuration (index 1, one voter), isolating the flagged recovery path as the cause.

experiments.revision_reason: Only the comparison declaration changes: identity_fields are reduced to the case selector (mode) so the startup_before_restart admission and the restart_after_recovery result share an identity; the harness, inputs and assertions are unchanged. The previous receipt correlated neither admission to a result, so its comparisons returned unknown even though the raw events were emitted.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading establishes the mechanism: NewRaft initialises configurations to its zero value, restoreSnapshot is the only producer that can supply a configuration from persistent state (api.go:655-681), and the only other producer is the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) starting at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1. restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs before that scan and calls setCommitIndex(commitIndex) then processLogs(commitIndex, nil); processLogs forwards LogConfiguration entries to the FSM (raft.go:1366-1391) and never updates r.configurations. With RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, every committed configuration entry at or below the restored commit index is therefore invisible to the node after restart. A native construction probe of a bootstrapped single node (CommitTrackingLogs, no snapshot, 10 applied entries) reproduced the predicted difference: with the flag on the event was {after_latest_index:0, after_servers:0, after_has_vote:false, after_commit_index:11, after_last_applied:11, before_latest_index:1, snapshots:0} and the library logged 'initial configuration: index=0 servers=[]'; with the flag off the same restart reported {after_latest_index:1, after_servers:1, after_has_vote:true}. The probe is construction feedback without a retained receipt, so the formal comparison is left to the submitted experiment. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node's own membership view is the pre-restart snapshot value or empty, so runFollower's 'no known peers, aborting election' branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) prevent it from campaigning, and quorumSize() is computed over a configuration that contradicts the committed log (raft.go:1087-1094). Counterevidence examined: a snapshot can legitimately supply the configuration (api.go:677-678) but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot; appendEntries processes only entries it newly appends (raft.go:1594-1621); leaderLoop only promotes latest to committed (raft.go:797-799). Limitations: the finding is scoped to the stated configuration and store conditions; the snapshot-present variant remains a registered gap; only a controller receipt can make this a completed comparison.

The retained receipt 99b89f1a9b634301a58130e5494d394f (exit 0) contains the four emitted events, and the two result events witness the predicted difference under identical inputs: event 1 (mode on, restore_committed_logs true, snapshots 0) reports after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false with after_commit_index 11 and after_last_applied 11, while event 3 (mode off) reports after_latest_index 1, after_servers 1, after_has_vote true. The admission events (0 and 2) confirm both cases started from before_latest_index 1 with one server, so the only difference is whether restoreFromCommittedLogs advanced lastApplied. Source reading explains the mechanism: NewRaft starts with an empty configurations struct, restoreSnapshot (api.go:655-681) is the only persistent-state producer of a configuration, and the startup log scan (api.go:610-613) is the only other producer but begins at max(snapshotIndex, lastApplied)+1; restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) runs first and sets lastApplied to the persisted commit index, so committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are skipped, and processLogs never updates r.configurations (raft.go:1366-1391). The receipt s declared comparisons returned unknown rather than violated: the controller reported "No corresponding prerequisite events reached: mode_on/startup_before_restart" for both on-case comparisons and the analogous message for the off-case control, because the compared identity included phase and the admission events carry phase before_restart while the result events carry after_restart. That is a declaration defect, not missing evidence, so the raw observations are retained and a successor experiment with identity_fields [mode] is submitted for a fresh, complete comparison; no completed comparison is claimed here. Consequence under the stated conditions: the restarted node holds an empty (or snapshot-age) membership view, so runFollower's "no known peers, aborting election" branch (raft.go:228-232) and the hasVote gate (raft.go:236-246) leave it unable to campaign, and quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) is computed over a configuration that contradicts its own committed log.
counterevidence: A restart without RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the configuration (event 3), which isolates the flagged recovery path rather than the restart itself.
A snapshot can supply a configuration (api.go:677-678), but only as of snapshot.ConfigurationIndex, which cannot cover a configuration committed after that snapshot.
limitations: The comparison outcomes in this receipt are unknown; a completed comparison waits on the successor experiment.
Only the single-node, no-snapshot case is witnessed; the snapshot-present variant remains the registered gap.
The separate suspicion that restoreFromCommittedLogs' processLogs call can block NewRaft before runFSM starts is untested and outside this claim.

result.summary: Completed the comparison with the corrected receipt. Receipt 3e2dd223dd5f43409c21066a1ca43175 shows both on-case comparisons violated (witness event index 1: after_latest_index 0, after_servers 0, after_has_vote false while commit index 11 and lastApplied 11 were restored over 12 log entries) and the off-case control holding (evaluated event index 3: index 1 with one voter), so the interpretation for investigation ef5ddbf78bd4456ea51537bd60a61a80-question-0 is now conclusion violated with defect_claim asserted, citing that receipt's decisive indices; the earlier uncorrelated receipt is retained as raw observations with explicit joint-history reasoning. Because RestoreCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before NewRaft's configuration scan (api.go:610-613, 724-754), committed LogConfiguration entries at or below it are never processed and the node returns with the snapshot's or an empty configuration, leaving it unable to campaign (raft.go:228-246) and computing quorum over a configuration contradicting its own log. A second experiment targets the open gap: with a snapshot present, committing an AddNonvoter change (then further entries so it falls below the restored commit index) reproduced the same loss locally (1 server and snapshot config index instead of 2 servers at index 62), and its receipt is still required before that variant is resolved; the gap answer is recorded with resolved=false.
